Changes in power-guard.py: the new _reap() and _… |
Full details: Title check

**Explanation** The title names the main change: power-guard now detects a dead systemd-inhibit child, re-engages it with logging, and reaps it on release. The diff matches each part of the title. The title is specific and accurate, and it fits the changeset.
Full details: Linked Issues check

**Explanation** Issue `#6534` is the only direct, active linked issue. Its coding requirements are met at head 2a6abfda. (1) Dead-child detection [`#6534`]: Inhibitor.held returns poll() is None for a real child. engage() calls _dead_exit_code() on an existing child. The change does not return early on a non-None proc. (2) Stated policy [`#6534`]: engage() logs 'INHIBIT child died (exit=rc); re-engaging', reaps the child, clears self.proc, and starts a new sleep infinity child. This is the re-engage option the issue allows. (3) Diagnosable failure [`#6534`]: the exit status is logged on death in engage() and in release(). The stderr=DEVNULL comment documents this choice. The issue accepts either stderr capture or exit-status logging, so this criterion is met. (4) release() reaps [`#6534`]: release() calls _reap() (wait with kill fallback) for a live child after terminate(). It reaps a dead child without terminate(). (5) Tests [`#6534`]: InhibitorDeadChildTests covers an immediately-dead child (detected, re-engaged, exit logged, reaped), a live child left undisturbed (no Popen call, no wait), the NO_INHIBIT stub path (held, engage, release unchanged), and release on live and dead children. (6) Existing tests [`#6534`]: the diff only adds code and tests. It does not modify the existing ParseTiming or DaemonSubprocess tests. The author reports 13 tests OK. I did not execute the suite, so this result relies on that report and on the unchanged existing tests. I verified these points by reading the whole-PR diff against the merge base and the test file at head. I did not run the tests. The real Popen path is not exercised end to end. The issue accepts unit-level coverage with a fake process.
Full details: Out of Scope Changes check

**Explanation** All changes are in nixos/services/power-guard/power-guard.py and nixos/services/power-guard/test_power_guard.py. Both files belong to the `#6534` scope. Changes in power-guard.py: the new _reap() and _dead_exit_code() helpers, the dead-child branch in engage(), the reworked release() with stub and real branches, the held property, and a comment on stderr. Each serves criteria (1) to (4) of `#6534`. Changes in test_power_guard.py: the FakeProc helper and InhibitorDeadChildTests. These are the tests the issue requests. The existing timing and daemon tests are unchanged. The stub path keeps its prior behavior. The one observable message change is that the real-child release now logs 'INHIBIT released (child exit=rc)'. This change supports the exit-status logging required by `#6534`. No unrelated behavior, file, or refactor appears in the diff.
Full details: Docstring Coverage

**Explanation** Docstring coverage is 25.00% which is insufficient. The required threshold is 80.00%. Docstring coverage is scoped to functions touched by this diff with cyclomatic complexity of at least 2. Documentation-only edits and deletions within surviving functions are included; unchanged diff context and fully deleted functions are excluded. Analyzed 8 functions across 2 files. **Resolution** Write docstrings for the functions missing them to satisfy the coverage threshold.

performed_via_github_app.description:
# Transforming Code Reviews with AI

## Features

**Automated Reviews**: Continuous reviews of the pull requests including incremental commits. 

**Summarization**: Generates high-level summary and a technical walkthrough of the PR changes. 

**Line-by-line review**: Provides line-by-line suggestions committable with one click.

**Codebase verification**:  Verifies the impact on the overall codebase and identifies missing changes.

**Insights into your code**:  Ask any questions on your codebase within the pull request 

**Chat about your code** : Chat with the bot around your code. The more you chat, the smarter it gets.

**Issue Validation**:  Validates the PR against the linked issues and identifies other related issues
